summary: Verified RevenueCat SDK integration on web preview. App bundles and loads cleanly with the new react-native-purchases + react-native-purchases-ui packages installed. Platform-split lib/revenuecat.web.ts stub correctly resolves for web via Metro's .web.ts extension convention, so react-native-purchases-ui (no web support) is never imported on web. Home 'Unlock Full Access' banner and Profile 'Unlock for £5.99' button both call openPaywall() which returns 'fallback' on web and correctly navigates to the custom /paywall screen. Paywall renders with all testIDs (close, purchase, restore). Tapping 'Get Premium — £5.99' in dev/web mode flips isPremium=true locally and router.back()s. After becoming premium, Profile shows 'Premium' badge, 'full access' success message, the NEW 'Manage Subscription' button (only when isPremium), and 'Restore Purchases'. Clicking 'Manage Subscription' on web is a safe no-op (openCustomerCenter early-returns because isRevenueCatConfigured=false), page does not crash. Regression: onboarding carousel Next flow works, Practice tab loads 14 categories, no console/page errors captured. Backend /api/health returns {status:ok}. Actual native RevenueCat purchase flow (react-native-purchases-ui presentPaywall / presentCustomerCenter / real App Store / Play Store purchases) is OUT OF SCOPE for this environment and NOT testable here — requires an EAS dev build on a physical iOS/Android device.
critical_code_review_comments: src/lib/revenuecat.ts line 1: `Platform` is imported from react-native but only used to pick iosKey vs androidKey. Since Metro resolves the .web.ts variant on web, the native file never runs on web — that is fine. However, if EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY were empty and Platform.OS returned something unexpected (e.g. 'windows'), isRevenueCatConfigured would silently be false. Consider logging when apiKey is empty on native for easier debugging on real devices.

src/stores/subscription-store.ts openPaywall(): when RevenueCatUI.presentPaywallIfNeeded throws on native, the catch sets an error and returns 'fallback', which will then push the custom /paywall on native too. That is a reasonable safety net but may hide real RevenueCat misconfigurations from surfacing to the user on device. Fine for MVP.

revenuecat.web.ts imports Purchases from 'react-native-purchases' but never actually calls Purchases.configure in getCustomerInfo (only in initializeRevenueCat which is only called with webKey.length===0 check). Since isRevenueCatConfigured is hardcoded false on web, this import is effectively dead code on web. Consider removing the Purchases import from revenuecat.web.ts to reduce web bundle size — react-native-purchases pulls a fair amount of native-adapter code even on web.

Native testing of presentPaywall / presentCustomerCenter / purchasePackage cannot be performed in this environment. Recommend running an EAS dev build (`eas build --profile development --platform ios/android`) on a physical device with the RevenueCat sandbox tester account before shipping.
context_for_next_testing_agent: RevenueCat is wired via platform-split modules (revenuecat.ts native / revenuecat.web.ts web). On web, isRevenueCatConfigured is hardcoded false and openPaywall() returns 'fallback' so calling code routes to /paywall. All testIDs exist: home-unlock-banner, profile-unlock-button, profile-manage-subscription-button (premium-only), profile-restore-button, paywall-close-button, paywall-purchase-button, paywall-restore-button. Zustand subscription store is NOT persisted across full page reloads, so after unlocking premium the state resets on hard nav — that is expected in dev/web (real device would use RevenueCat's CustomerInfo which is server-persisted). Native purchase flow requires EAS dev build to test — do not attempt on web.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found in the tested scope.
